case_name: Dev Narayan and Others v State of Madhya Pradesh and Others
facts: The case is about nine accused who were convicted for various crimes including murder and sentenced to life imprisonment.
The complainant Dinesh Singh is Thakur by caste and is resident of village Hasnabad.
There was long standing enmity between Dinesh Singh and his family members on the one side and persons of Khati community on the other side.
Panchayat elections had taken place 3-4 months prior to the incident in which Raju @ Rajesh Prajapati accused won the election.

The case of the prosecution is that the deceased Sardar was unwell and he was brought to the house of the complainant Dinesh Singh in the afternoon of 1.9.1994 so that some medical aid could be provided to him.
The complainant Dinesh Singh took the deceased Sardar on his scooter to Sehore Government Hospital sometime before 6.00 P.M.
When he had taken a turn on Hasnabad road from the side of Echhavar road, which is about four kilometers from Sehore, he saw eleven accused armed with various weapons standing there.
issues: Whether the conviction of the accused is proper?
Whether the evidence of the prosecution is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that their false implication on account of enmity.
They denied the prosecution case and alleged their false implication on account of enmity.
respondent_arguments: The State argued that the evidence of the prosecution is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused.
court_reasoning: The court held that the testimony of PW-1 Dinesh Singh has to be assessed with care and caution.
The court found that the active participation of four accused in the incident in question is fully established.
The court gave benefit of doubt to remaining accused by way of abundant caution.
holding: The appeal filed by the appellant No. 1 Dev Narayan, appellant No. 3 Ghisi Lal Khati and appellant No. 7 Hari Narayan Khati is dismissed.

The appeal filed by appellant No. 2 Ramesh Khati, appellant No. 4 Raju @ Rajesh Prajapati, appellant No. 5 Laxmi Narayan, appellant No. 6 Bhanwar Lal, appellant No. 8 Rajesh Verma Khati and appellant No. 9 Babu Lal is allowed.
The conviction of the aforesaid appellants and the sentences imposed upon them are set aside.
cases_cited: Dev Narayan and Others v State of Madhya Pradesh
